F1.quote: The Bodmer Lab, a hub for research and digitisation born out of a partnership between the University of Geneva and the Martin Bodmer Foundation, has made a significant number of these rare and fragile documents available to the public.
F1.claim: the Lab by its own About page: a hub for research and digitisation from a partnership of the University of Geneva and the Martin Bodmer Foundation, which has made many rare and fragile documents of the collection public
F1.lineage: what it is: a digital library, a research and digitization project of a partnership

F2.quote: Supported by the Fondation Ernst and Lucie Schmidheiny. … It was able to grow thanks to the exceptional support of the Fondation Ernst and Lucie Schmidheiny.
F2.claim: the Lab supported by the Fondation Ernst and Lucie Schmidheiny, and grown by its exceptional support
F2.lineage: who makes it: the direction and the support
F2.checked_against: saved text B1.txt (sha256 d35535c54707854a…), whitespace-normalised; multi-part quote, each part checked

F3.quote: The Martin Bodmer Foundation maintains a unique collection of inscriptions, manuscripts and printed documents, from the oldest examples of writing up through the present day, chosen for their status as remarkable evidence of human thought and creativity.
F3.claim: the Foundation's collection: inscriptions, manuscripts and printed documents from the oldest writing to the present, chosen as evidence of human thought and creativity
F3.lineage: the partner: the Fondation Martin Bodmer and its library

F4.quote: The Bodmer Lab uses new technology to bring to the fore the structure of this unique “library of world literature.”
F4.claim: the Lab uses new technology to bring out the structure of the 'library of world literature'
F4.lineage: world literature: Martin Bodmer's library, its principle and lineage

F5.quote: Through videos, images libraries, digital stores and games, the Bodmer Lab also speaks to a wider audience, schoolchildren, explorers and lovers of learning.
F5.claim: it also addresses a wider audience through videos, image libraries, digital stories and games
F5.lineage: the bets: materiality, selection, smart data, constellations, audiences

F6.quote: The Bibliotheca Bodmeriana was conceived by Martin Bodmer as a “library of world literature.” We decided to take this intellectual ambition seriously and make it the guiding principle of the Bodmer Lab.
F6.claim: the governing principle: Martin Bodmer's conception of the Bibliotheca Bodmeriana as a 'library of world literature', taken as the Lab's guiding principle
F6.lineage: world literature: Martin Bodmer's library, its principle and lineage

F7.quote: We have prioritised the materiality of the works, which is why we have planned to use Optical Character Recognition (OCR) later rather than sooner: this way, the texts come into view through the lens of their editorial editions.
F7.claim: materiality prioritised: OCR planned later rather than sooner, so the texts are seen through their editions
F7.lineage: the bets: materiality, selection, smart data, constellations, audiences

F8.quote: The Bodmer collection is nearly endless, and it seemed unrealistic to us to begin to digitise it all straightaway. Exhaustiveness can actually be misleading when put into practice.
F8.claim: the stated limit: the collection is not digitised whole; exhaustiveness can mislead
F8.lineage: the bets: materiality, selection, smart data, constellations, audiences

F9.quote: When commentaries which highlight the cultural significance of these data are added to the equation, we are instead dealing in the realm of “ smart data .”
F9.claim: the defined term 'smart data': digitised data with commentary on their cultural significance
F9.lineage: the bets: materiality, selection, smart data, constellations, audiences

F10.quote: In order to better appreciate the value of these strong points in the collection, we have approached them as “constellations,” partially autonomous and requiring specific subject knowledge. Consequently, we have decided to entrust the scientific supervision of each to internationally-recognised specialists in the given field.
F10.claim: the defined term 'constellations': strong points of the collection, partially autonomous, each under internationally recognised specialists
F10.lineage: the bets: materiality, selection, smart data, constellations, audiences

F11.quote: Each holding has its own particularities: papyri that are more than two thousand years old require different technological treatment than editions of Faust from the 19 th century.
F11.claim: papyri more than two thousand years old require different technological treatment from nineteenth-century editions
F11.lineage: the bets: materiality, selection, smart data, constellations, audiences

F12.quote: Michel Jeanneret (1940-2019) … Radu Suciu … Jérôme David
F12.claim: the direction: Michel Jeanneret (1940–2019), Radu Suciu, Jérôme David
F12.lineage: who makes it: the direction and the support
F12.checked_against: saved text B1.txt (sha256 d35535c54707854a…), whitespace-normalised; multi-part quote, each part checked

F13.quote: Online catalog of the papyrus and parchment manuscripts in the Bodmer collection
F13.claim: the Bodmer Papyri constellation: an online catalogue of the collection's papyrus and parchment manuscripts
F13.lineage: the Bodmer Papyri constellation: catalogue, aim, count, numbering, supervision

F14.quote: The majority of these were acquired by Martin Bodmer in the 1950s and early 1960s.
F14.claim: most acquired by Martin Bodmer in the 1950s and early 1960s
F14.lineage: the papyri: holdings, acquisition, provenance, dispersal

F15.quote: Many of these items seem to have formed part of a larger ancient collection that included works in Greek, Coptic, and Latin (though only Greek and Coptic are represented in the Bodmer collection).
F15.claim: many seem to have formed part of a larger ancient collection in Greek, Coptic and Latin; only Greek and Coptic in the Bodmer collection
F15.lineage: the papyri: holdings, acquisition, provenance, dispersal

F16.quote: While a number of the books contain interesting combinations of Christian works (such as PB 3, a codex containing the Gospel According to John and part of Genesis in Coptic), there are also classical books, such as the Menander codex (PB M).
F16.claim: Christian works (PB 3: John and part of Genesis in Coptic) and classical books (PB M, the Menander codex)
F16.lineage: the papyri: holdings, acquisition, provenance, dispersal

F17.quote: Other manuscripts contain both classical and Christian material, such as PB T, a codex that includes parts of the biblical book of Daniel in Greek along with book 6 of Thucydides, among other texts.
F17.claim: codices mixing classical and Christian material (PB T: Daniel in Greek with Thucydides book 6)
F17.lineage: the papyri: holdings, acquisition, provenance, dispersal

F18.quote: These manuscripts are of course highly important for the history of early Christianity, and because of the excellent state of preservation of many of the codices, they are of exceptional interest for historians of the book as well.
F18.claim: the manuscripts highly important for the history of early Christianity and, by their preservation, for historians of the book
F18.lineage: the earliest New Testament papyri among them

F19.quote: We employ a numbering system that uses the abbreviation PB (Papyrus Bodmer) and an Arabic number or a Latin letter. In most cases, these numbers correspond to the older system of Roman numerals: P.Bodmer I = PB1; P.Bodmer II = PB 2, etc.
F19.claim: the catalogue's numbering: PB with an Arabic number or a Latin letter, mostly matching the Roman P.Bodmer numerals
F19.lineage: the Bodmer Papyri constellation: catalogue, aim, count, numbering, supervision

F28.quote: Le Bodmer Lab tâche de résoudre une équation à trois variables : comment valoriser une collection privée exceptionnelle en tenant compte de son projet intellectuel d’ensemble et avec l’appui des nouvelles technologies ?
F28.claim: the Lab's purpose: how to valorise an exceptional private collection with its intellectual project, with new technology
F28.lineage: world literature: Martin Bodmer's library, its principle and lineage

F29.quote: Les documents numérisés de la Bibliotheca Bodmeriana se trouvent ici accompagnés de savoirs et d’outils qui visent à les réinscrire dans leur époque et, plus largement, dans cette « bibliothèque de la littérature mondiale » dont rêvait Martin Bodmer.
F29.claim: the digitised documents accompanied by knowledge and tools to re-inscribe them in their time and in Bodmer's 'library of world literature'
F29.lineage: world literature: Martin Bodmer's library, its principle and lineage

F30.quote: Sauf indication contraire, les contenus de ce site sont publiés sous une licence Creative commons CC-BY-NC, 4.0.

F31.quote: Bodmer a d’abord envisagé sa collection comme une histoire de l’esprit humain sur quatre millénaires avant qu’il ne vienne à la considérer, dès l’avènement de Hitler au pouvoir, comme l’un des seuls refuges possibles d’un humanisme préservé des mythes nazis.
F31.claim: Jérôme David's essay: Bodmer first conceived the collection as a history of the human spirit over four millennia, then, from Hitler's coming to power, as a refuge of a humanism preserved from Nazi myths
F31.lineage: world literature: Martin Bodmer's library, its principle and lineage
F31.date: undated essay announced on the home page (read 2026-10-31)

F32.quote: La Fondation vous accueille pour un voyage à travers cinq millénaires d’histoire de l’écrit.
F32.claim: the Fondation's span: five millennia of the history of writing
F32.lineage: the partner: the Fondation Martin Bodmer and its library

F33.quote: La Fondation Martin Bodmer est à la fois une bibliothèque patrimoniale exceptionnelle – inscrite au programme Mémoire du monde de l’UNESCO –, un lieu de recherche et de conservation, ainsi qu’un musée ouvert à tous, dédié à l’écrit, des origines de l’écriture jusqu’à nos jours.

F37.quote: The library was established by [[Martin Bodmer]] and is famous as the home of the [[Bodmer Papyri]]. Some of these papyri are among the oldest remaining copies of the [[New Testament]].

F39.quote: Martin Bodmer established the library in the 1920s. Bodmer selected the works centering on what he saw as the five pillars of [[world literature]]: the [[Bible]], [[Homer]], [[Dante Alighieri]], [[William Shakespeare]] and [[Johann Wolfgang von Goethe]].
F39.claim: established in the 1920s around the five pillars of world literature: the Bible, Homer, Dante, Shakespeare, Goethe
F39.lineage: world literature: Martin Bodmer's library, its principle and lineage

F40.quote: In 1970, shortly before Bodmer's death, the Bodmer Foundation was established to make the collection accessible and conserve it.

F41.quote: The collection comprises some 160,000 items, including Sumerian clay tablets, Greek papyri and handwritten originals including music sheets.
F41.claim: some 160,000 items, Sumerian tablets, Greek papyri and autographs among them
F41.lineage: the partner: the Fondation Martin Bodmer and its library

F42.quote: A copy of Shakespeare's [[First Folio]], 1623, in its original binding. Digitised by [http://bodmerlab.unige.ch The Bodmer Lab], this copy is available
F42.claim: the encyclopedia's one naming of the entity: the First Folio of 1623, digitised by The Bodmer Lab

F43.quote: [[Papyrus 66]] (near-complete codex of the Gospel of John), [[Papyrus 73]] and [[Papyrus 74]] (Acts and Catholic epistles)
F43.claim: among the items P66 (a near-complete codex of John), P73 and P74
F43.lineage: the earliest New Testament papyri among them

F44.quote: The '''Dishna Papers''', also often known as the '''Bodmer Papyri''', are a group of twenty-two [[papyri]] discovered in [[Dishna, Egypt]] in 1952. Later, they were purchased by [[Martin Bodmer]] and deposited at the [[Bodmer Library]] in Switzerland.
F44.claim: Wikipedia ('Bodmer Papyri' redirects here): the Dishna Papers, twenty-two papyri found at Dishna, Egypt, in 1952, bought by Martin Bodmer
F44.lineage: the papyri: holdings, acquisition, provenance, dispersal

F45.quote: {{about|22 papyri discovered in Egypt in 1952, purchased by Martin Bodmer|a list of the 58 papyri in Bodmer's collection|List of Bodmer Papyri}}
F45.claim: a list of 58 papyri in Bodmer's collection
F45.lineage: the papyri: holdings, acquisition, provenance, dispersal

F46.quote: The papyri contain segments from the Old and New Testaments, early Christian literature, [[Homer]], and [[Menander]]. The oldest, [[Papyrus 66|P<sup>66</sup>]], dates to {{circa|200 AD}}.
F46.claim: the papyri's contents (Old and New Testament, early Christian literature, Homer, Menander); the oldest, P66, c. 200 AD
F46.lineage: the earliest New Testament papyri among them

F47.quote: Since the papers are held not only at the Bodmer Library, but also at the Vatican, Oslo, Barcelona, and other locations, many scholars have preferred the term ''Dishna Papers'' since the mid-2010s.
F47.claim: held also at the Vatican, Oslo, Barcelona and elsewhere; many scholars prefer 'Dishna Papers' since the mid-2010s
F47.lineage: the papyri: holdings, acquisition, provenance, dispersal

F48.quote: In 2007, the [[Vatican Library]] acquired Bodmer Papyrus 14–15 (known as [[Papyrus 75|P<sup>75</sup>]] and as the Mater Verbi ([[Frank Hanna III|Hanna]]) Papyrus).
F48.claim: P75 (Bodmer Papyrus 14–15) acquired by the Vatican Library in 2007
F48.lineage: the papyri: holdings, acquisition, provenance, dispersal

F49.quote: [[Papyrus 66]] (P<sup>66</sup>), is a text of the [[Gospel of John]], … dating around 200 AD, in the manuscript tradition called the [[Alexandrian text-type]].
F49.claim: P66 a text of John, c. 200 AD, Alexandrian text-type
F49.lineage: the earliest New Testament papyri among them
F49.checked_against: saved text B13.txt (sha256 1f024894b4a6ec48…), whitespace-normalised; multi-part quote, each part checked

F50.quote: [[Papyrus 72|𝔓<sup>72</sup>]] is the earliest known copy of the [[Epistle of Jude]], and 1 and 2 Peter. … [[Papyrus 75]] (P<sup>75</sup>) is a partial codex containing most of Luke and John.
F50.claim: P72 the earliest known copy of Jude and 1–2 Peter; P75 a partial codex of most of Luke and John
F50.lineage: the earliest New Testament papyri among them
F50.checked_against: saved text B13.txt (sha256 1f024894b4a6ec48…), whitespace-normalised; multi-part quote, each part checked

F51.quote: Comparison of the two versions of John in the Bodmer Papyri with the third-century [[Chester Beatty Papyri]] convinced Floyd V. Filson that "...there was no uniform text of the Gospels in Egypt in the third century."
F51.claim: Filson: the two Bodmer texts of John against the Chester Beatty papyri show no uniform text of the Gospels in third-century Egypt
F51.lineage: the earliest New Testament papyri among them

F52.quote: The latest of the Bodmer Papyri (P<sup>74</sup>) dates to the sixth or seventh century.
F52.claim: the latest, P74, sixth or seventh century
F52.lineage: the earliest New Testament papyri among them

F53.quote: Lundhaug (2018) argues that the Dishna Papers in fact came from the same monastic library as the [[Nag Hammadi library]].
F53.claim: Lundhaug (2018): the Dishna Papers from the same monastic library as the Nag Hammadi codices
F53.lineage: the papyri: holdings, acquisition, provenance, dispersal
